subject: Media Literacy
title: Dark Patterns in Privacy Settings
description: A quick win: understand Dark Patterns in Privacy Settings.

hook.text: A privacy pop-up has 'Accept All' in bright green and 'Manage Settings' in tiny grey text. The design is deliberate.

buildup.text: Dark patterns are user interface designs that trick people into making choices they wouldn't otherwise make.

discovery.text: In privacy settings, dark patterns include confusing language, buried opt-outs, and guilt-tripping decline messages.

twist.text: Regulators required consent. Companies responded by making consent harder to refuse than to give.

climax.text: When 'no' takes 15 clicks and 'yes' takes one, consent is engineered, not freely given.

punchline.text: If rejecting takes more effort than accepting, the design is the manipulation.

quiz.question: What are dark patterns in privacy settings?
options: Privacy settings with dark color themes
Interface designs that trick users into giving up more privacy than intended
Settings that only appear at night
